Passage 1
 School Uniforms
1    There are no clear records to show when the wearing of school uniforms really started but this 
 tradition has certainly been around for hundreds of years. In the Unlted States, it was observed 
 that more schools started to implement uniforms after President Bill Clinton pitched for the use 
 of school uniforms in hls 1996 State of the Union Address. The move was met with mixed 
 reactions as some parties saw it as an irritation for students while others viewed it as   5 
 the solution to improve the educational system and performance of school children.
2     Uniforms create a better sense of unity because everyone will wear the same clothes and have a single identity. There will also be less competition among children as to who has 
 the most stylish outfits. When everyone is dressed the same and feels proud to be a part of their 
 school, it boosts morale.      10 
3     School uniforms can usually be worn for a whole year or two. This allows parents to save on 
 time and money spent on shopping for school clothes as there is no need to buy new clothes 
 for every semester. Moreover parents do not have to deal with choosy offspring who demand 
 expensive brands. A uniform enables students to spend less time and energy on choosing 
 what to wear daily; thus getting ready for school in the morning will be easier and faster.      15 
4     Uniforms help to remove social segregation. The way you dress usually indicates what sort of 
 clique you belong to. If everyone is dressed the same, it can take away the need t0 put a label 
 on each person and as such it can provide a more sociable school environment . If children 
 cannot show their individuallty through clothes, they may well express themselves through 
 other methods such as the arts, academics sports, or extra-curricular activities.     20 
5     However, no-one Is in any doubt that school uniforms can be annoying. They take away the 
 opportunity to develop a sense of individuality and freedom of expression, somothing which 
 most parents want their children to learn from a young age. By not being allowed to show their 
 individuallty through the way they dress, children may feel discouraged to develop their own 
 personality. Everyone will agree that this creates an unnecessary strain for the chlldren      25
6     Uniforms can be an additional cost If children go to school 5 or 6 days a week, they need at 
 least 2-3 sets of uniforms. Thls can cause extra stress to students and parents. Familles that 
 cannot afford several sets of uniforms may have to wash the uniforms when the children get 
 home. 
7     Some children may feel uncomfortable due to the rlgidity and this can affect their mood and     30 
 learning throughout the whole day. As most schools educate students from many different 
 cultures, the imposition of one style of dress which can only represent one culture may 
 cause resentment and an intolerance of other cultures. 
8     Despite the  good   intention,  uniforms   undermine   free   education. Unless the school or 
 govemment will sponsor the cost of uniforms, it will be the students' families who need to 
 shoulder the expense. And this contradicts the idea of free education since public schools are 
 supposed to provide education at no cost to parents. Families will resent this and such parental 
 dissent, coupled with cultural intolerance, may well give rise to poor academic performance, 
 decreasing attendance and even violence, some of the major issues that schools too often 
 face today.     40

Passage 2
 A reformed convict
1    A guard came to the prison shop where Jimmy Valentine 9762 was busy stitching 
 leather bags and escorted him to the front office. There the warden handed him a pardon, 
 remarking. "Stop cracking safes, son, and live straight He had served ten months out of 
 a four-year sentence. The next morning, Jimmy was a free man.  
2     He walked with quick, springing steps, his left hand hanging freely by the side of his coat.     5 
 The coat had once been white , but now it was worn-out and torn: His right hand held onto 
 a string which carried a small parcel on his bent back. The parcel was well wrapped with 
 a cotton cloth which had once been printed with red flowers, although the flowers could 
 now hardly be seen. The parcel swung from side to side with every stride. It held the 
 unhappiness and pain of the months in prison. Now and then he looked at the sun on its     10 
 journey home. Sometimes he threw quick glances to the side, at the houses with their neatly cut hedges. 
3     Five hours later, he got off a train at a small country town. He walked into Mike Dolan's 
 cafe , took a key and went upstairs. The room was just as he had left it. Pulling out from 
 the wall his folding bed, Jimmy slid back a panel in the wall and dragged out a dust-covered     15 
 suitcase. He opened it and gazed fondly at the finest set of burglars' tools ever made. Then 
 he changed his suit, took his suitcase and disappeared. 
4     A week after his release, there began a alarming series of safe burglaries. Detective 
 Inspector Ben Price began the investigation and concluded that he knew of only one 
 person who would be able to judge when safes would contain such vast sums of money    20
 and could crack a safe with such precision. This time he would be shown no leniency or 
 pardon. 
5     One afternoon , Jimmy and his suitcase arrived In Elmore. On the way to his hotel, he was passed by a very attractive lady who entered the Elmore Bank: When Jimmy looked into 
 her eyes, he instantly forgot the man he was ad became another man. It so happened    25 
 that the lady was Anabel Adams, the bank manager's daughter. So, Jimmy remained in 
 Elmore , opened a shoe-store under the name of Robert Spencer and prospered, Within a 
 year, he was engaged to Anabel. Shortly before the marriage, he wrote to a trusted ex- 
 prison friend in distant St Louis. If he met the 9 pm. train next Monday, Jimmy would 
 present him with the set of tools he now no longer needed. The excuse he gave his friend.    30 
 In Elmore was that he wanted to order his wedding suit and buy a gift for his beloved 
 Anabel. 
6     On the morning of his departure , Jimmy took his suitcase ad had breakfast with the 
 Adams family. Then Mr Adams invited him and his family down to the bank where a new 
 safe and vault had been installed. In order to shut the safe, a timer would be set for the    35 
 safe's opening, after which the safe's three steel bolts would automatically close as soon 
 as the door was shut. As they strolled around, there was a sudden scream from Mrs 
 Adams, May, the nine-year-old daughter, had shut her younger sister Agatha in the vault. 
 The timer had not been set and although they all tugged frantically at the knob it was in 
 vain. Inside they heard the faint screams of the imprisoned child who would soon be     40 
 suffocated. 
7     "Can't you do something, Robert try, won't you?" said Anabel pleadingly. With that, 
 Robert Spencer passed away and Jimmy Valentine took his place. In hushed silence, 
 he opened his suitcase flal, revealing rows of shining weird implements. Soon his pet drill 
 was biting smoothly into the steel door. In ten minutes, he threw back the bolts and the door    45 
 swung open. Jimmy then put on his coat and walked silently out.
8     As he stepped into the street, a well-known voice called "Robert:" It was Ben Price. 
 "Hello, Ben" said Jimmy: "I guess the game is up! Let's go! 
 " "Guess you are mistaken , Mr Spencer;" said Ben, "I don't know you. Your taxi is waiting to 
 take you to the station.      50 
 And Ben Price turned and strolled down the street alone.
